current.text: The projected starters are James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen.
Cleveland lost Dennis Schroder, Max Strus, Keon Ellis and Dean Wade, all rotation players.
The projected bench is Jaylon Tyson, Sam Merrill, Thomas Bryant, Nae'Qwan Tomlin and Craig Porter Jr.
Bench depth is weak after those losses, so Jaylon Tyson must play a lot.
Big-man depth is very poor. Behind Mobley and Allen there is only Thomas Bryant, then Ernest Udeh Jr. and Khalifa Diop.
Losing Dean Wade also removes the small-ball center option.
Cleveland may close games with Mobley at center now that Watson is on the team. It is not clear yet whether Kenny Atkinson will lean on those smaller lineups or on Allen and Harden pick-and-rolls.
The second unit has no clear point guard, so Harden and Mitchell may stagger their minutes.
How much Harden and Mitchell play together is the key question for Mitchell's value.
Harden is with the team full time, so more players need the ball. His usage dropped in Cleveland, and his arrival cut into Mitchell's assists and scoring.
The backcourt is crowded with Harden and Mitchell, who signed an extension, so there is no immediate role for rookies.
There are no current injury concerns on the team.
Cleveland is a very good team. One expert predicts about 51 to 53 wins, above the market win total.
Coach Kenny Atkinson is under pressure.
Cleveland has among the most back-to-backs in the league, so rest risk for its stars is higher.
The fantasy playoff schedule is the worst in the league: 4, 3 and 2 games in weeks 19 to 21, with only 2 games in finals week (the week starting March 22).
From December 23 to February 6 the schedule has no consecutive home or road games, so heavy travel could hurt the team.

note: Cleveland projects as a winning team, but its fantasy playoff schedule is the worst in the league (9 games, only 2 in finals week), and it has among the most back-to-backs. That is a reason to pay less for Mitchell, Harden, Mobley and Allen, who also share the ball. The thin bench and very poor big-man depth make Jaylon Tyson and Thomas Bryant worth watching. Early on, watch how much Harden and Mitchell play together and whether Atkinson closes games with Mobley at center.
